provenance.author: block writer B2 (Claude Opus 5.5, model-written)
notes: Narration is now in the past (preterite for events). No imperfect (roedd) is used anywhere: description is carried by 'gwelodd e X yn …', verbless phrases and dialogue in the present. Group actions use noun subjects with 3sg verbs (Daeth y milwyr …, Gadawodd y milwyr …). Plural pronoun subjects in the past are avoided (Pennod 23).

Selected 3sg verbs: daeth, aeth, cafodd, gwnaeth; -odd on hedfan, gweld, edrych, codi, troi, glanio, disgyn, cyrraedd, gadael, cuddio, gwenu, rhedeg, cofio. Irregular stems not derivable by the checker's suffix rule are licensed as forms in the delta (gwelodd, trodd, cyrhaeddodd, gadawodd, disgynnodd; aeth/daeth/cafodd/gwnaeth also recorded as cy-mynd/dod/cael/gwneud forms), and 'past' card stages are added for mynd, dod, cael, gwneud and gweld (§8.3).

Do / Naddo answer only simple-past questions (Welaist ti …? Gest ti …? Wnest ti …?); the Ydw / Nac ydw contrast is set beside them in the same scene (Wyt ti'n flinedig? — Ydw). No inflected past negatives are used.

Prior coverage sits at the 88% floor because the target forms themselves (gwelodd, aeth, daeth, trodd …) count as new tokens; the hawk is called 'yr hen aderyn' in places to keep the new noun hebog from dominating.
Section count 4 as planned (the take-off and the flight over the valley share one section). 'i lawr' lemma-validation warning concerns the planned phrase lexeme.
Dafi's short sentence 'Dafi'n ofni hebog!' (s027) is Rhan 2 Dafi-speech, not a flagged deliberate error; the Codex review (2026-10-12) accepts it as the established fragment convention.

Codex review 2026-10-12, verdicts on the [?] questions (all accepted, no text change): s011 'trodd Arth yn hebog'; s031 'Gwelodd e olau'r haul' (object SM on the head noun golau); s035 'Mae Cwm Helyg yn wahanol o'r awyr: map yw e!'; s046 standard spelling cyrhaeddodd; s038 disgyn (plymio unnecessary); s075 'Fi yw hebog Cynyr' as plain identification; s126 purpose 'i ffeindio bwyd' (ff does not mutate); s041 'i'r coed'.

Applied from the Codex review (2026-10-12): s044 drops the singular 'Paid ag ofni!' (addressed to a nest of birds; peidiwch is not yet available) and keeps 'Dw i ddim yn benhwyad! Arth dw i!'; nodyn_en states object SM after the verb and its subject; B.b5 accepts cwmwl, B.b7 adain; C.c2 and C.c6 accept full-sentence answers; A.a1–a5 accept the supplied ddoe/neithiwr cue; the wedi recall cue is now '(wedi)' rather than '(nawr: wedi)'.

Recall pass 2026-10-18: recurrences added for cy-ph-go-iawn (s012 'hebog go iawn'), cy-ph-dim-ond (s120, Myrddin's evasion), cy-byw (s076, the old hawk), cy-ph-yn-gyntaf / cy-ph-yn-olaf (s016, s087, framing the flight). Padding: retired s134 (a third consecutive line restating the hawk; s128 carries the same beat). Gloss symbols: disgyn '↓ ↓ ↓' → 'mynd i lawr'; clymu '= ∞' → '→ un'.
Critique pass 2026-10-18 (docs/reviews/recall-pass-critique-2026-10-18.md): s105 reverted to HEAD (Arth no longer has wings).

Audit-fix pass 2026-10-19: s017 i fyny no longer glossed with i lawr before i lawr is met (now 'i fyny = ↑'; the i lawr ↔ i fyny pair sits on i lawr's first use, s031). Gramadeg: untaught 'dim newid' replaced by 'gwelodd e'r cysgod (c → c)'. Pensa A.a7, A.a8, C.c2 accept full answers (Ydw, dw i'n flinedig; Do. Gwelais i'r dieithryn; Do. Gwelodd e Dafi).

grammar.nodyn_en: The story is now told in the past. For he/she add -odd to the stem: hedfanodd, gwelodd, glaniodd. Four common verbs are irregular: aeth, daeth, cafodd, gwnaeth. A bare noun object after the verb and its subject softens (gwelodd e filwyr; cafodd Arth gawl). Answer a simple-past question with Do (yes) or Naddo (no), not Ydw / Nac ydw.

card_stages.back: yes (answer to a simple-past question: Welaist ti …? — Do.)
no (answer to a simple-past question: Gest ti …? — Naddo.)
to go — I went, he went
to come — I came, he came
to get, have — I got, he got

card_stages.front: Hedfanodd Arth. Gwelodd e filwyr. — Welaist ti'r ogof? — Do. / Naddo.
card_stages.back: Arth flew. He saw soldiers. — Did you see the cave? — Yes. / No. (aeth, daeth, cafodd, gwnaeth)
